ventral_fluke_pixel_intensity_distributi.global_contrast_ratio: Extremely low white-to-black ratio; approximately 95% of the visible surface consists of low-intensity dark gray/black pixels, with high-intensity white pixels restricted to localized anomalies and distal tips.
ventral_fluke_pixel_intensity_distributi.spatial_color_mapping: Uniformly dark pixel field across the central and proximal fluke regions. High-contrast white geometric blobs are localized as small circular clusters at the distal tips and specific isolated coordinates on the lobe surfaces.

trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.median_notch_angle: Deep, symmetrical V-shaped notch with an approximate vertex angle of 45-55 degrees, showing a clear pixel-level separation between the left and right lobes.
trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.edge_topography_serration_map: Highly irregular and serrated trailing edge. The right lobe exhibits higher amplitude peaks and deeper valleys compared to the left, with significant pixel-level jaggedness distal to the median notch.
trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.lobe_sweep_trajectory: Trailing edges exhibit a concave curve leading from the median notch to the tips; leading edges (partially visible) suggest a convex sweep toward the distal terminals.

localized_surface_anomalies.rosette_scar_constellations: Dense clusters of high-contrast, roughly circular pixel formations (barnacle colonies) are prominent on the far left and far right distal tips.
localized_surface_anomalies.linear_abrasions: One distinct, high-intensity diagonal linear mark is visible on the upper section of the right lobe; a second, smaller vertical linear disruption is visible near the center-left of the left lobe.

acquired_anomalies_or_scars: Extensive biological encrustations (barnacles) on both distal tips; distinct irregular indentations and a deep secondary notch on the trailing edge of the right lobe.
other_distinctive_markers: Vertical trails of high-intensity pixel points (water droplets) are visible shedding from the trailing edge of the left lobe.
